health: YELLOW — The core architecture (ServiceLocator + EventBus + Bootstrap) is solid, well-documented, and follows disciplined separation of concerns. Gameplay loop (snake movement, energy collection, detection, scoring, level progression) is functional in a single-scene model. However, the project is missing critical menus (MainMenu, Pause, GameOver, Options), has a commented-out pause handler, a no-op RemoveListener in the EventBus, invalid [SerializeField] on a plain C# class (InputManager), and Level_01.unity is not in Build Settings. The prototype plays in-editor but cannot ship as a standalone build without menu scaffolding and the blocker fixes below.

top_tasks.title: Add Level_01 to Build Settings and set as entry scene
top_tasks.reason: Only SampleScene is in Build Settings — a standalone build would boot into the wrong (or empty) scene.

top_tasks.title: Implement Pause system (uncomment + wire PauseInputEvent)
top_tasks.reason: OnPause handler body is commented out; pressing Escape/P/Start does nothing, making the game uninterruptible.

top_tasks.title: Create MainMenu UI overlay (UXML + USS) with Play / Quit buttons
top_tasks.reason: GameState.MainMenu exists in the enum but no UI or logic drives it — the game jumps straight into gameplay.

top_tasks.title: Create GameOver / Retry overlay with score summary
top_tasks.reason: AlertOverlay partially covers this but lacks a proper score recap, highscore display integration, or return-to-menu flow.

top_tasks.title: Fix InputManager [SerializeField] on non-MonoBehaviour
top_tasks.reason: InputManager is a plain C# class (IGameService) using [Header] and [SerializeField] which are MonoBehaviour-only attributes — they silently do nothing and mislead readers.

top_tasks.title: Fix GameEventManager.RemoveListener (currently a no-op)
top_tasks.reason: UIManager.Shutdown calls RemoveListener 8 times but the method body is empty, causing listener leaks on scene reload or service re-init.

blockers.title: Level_01.unity missing from EditorBuildSettings
blockers.detail: Build Settings only contains SampleScene.unity. A standalone build will not load Level_01 at all, resulting in a blank/wrong scene on launch.

blockers.title: No entry-point menu or game-start flow
blockers.detail: GameState.MainMenu is defined but never triggered. The game auto-starts gameplay on Awake with no user-facing start screen, violating every platform's UX certification requirement.

blockers.title: Confirm action hardwired to RespawnEvent
blockers.detail: InputManager line 56 permanently maps Enter/Space/A-button to RespawnEvent regardless of game state. This will respawn the player during gameplay, during menus, during level intros — completely breaking flow.

quick_checks.main_menu_exists: NO — GameState.MainMenu enum value exists but no UI/scene/logic implements it.
quick_checks.pause_exists: NO — PauseInputEvent event class exists, input bindings exist, but OnPause handler is commented out. No Time.timeScale logic anywhere.
quick_checks.options_menu_exists_audio: NO — AudioManager service is registered but no UI exposes volume sliders or audio settings.
quick_checks.options_menu_exists_controls: NO — No rebinding UI or control settings exist.
quick_checks.multi_controller_support: YES (partial) — InputManager binds Gamepad leftStick, dpad, and start button alongside keyboard. Multiple simultaneous controllers are not disambiguated.
quick_checks.mobile_input_mapping: NO — No Touchscreen bindings, no virtual joystick, no swipe detection anywhere in the codebase.
quick_checks.single_scene_loader_pattern: YES — Zero calls to SceneManager.LoadScene in the entire codebase. All state transitions are handled via GameState enum + UI overlay toggling within a single scene.

quick_fix: Uncomment line 98 in InputManager.cs (`GameEventManager.Publish(new PauseInputEvent())`) and add a 5-line handler in GameBootstrapper.Update or a new tiny PauseService that toggles Time.timeScale between 0 and 1 on PauseInputEvent, plus show/hide a 'PAUSED' label in UIManager.OnGameStateChanged for GameState.Paused. This gives you a working pause in under 30 minutes, making the in-editor experience feel like a shippable game loop. For the remaining 30 minutes, add Level_01 to Build Settings and wire the LevelIntro overlay to show on first boot as a pseudo-main-menu (title + Begin button already exist in UXML).
